title: Measuring Emergent Misalignment in Mixture-of-Experts Models Versus Dense Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Architecture-specific misalignment analysis is interesting but somewhat niche. Expert localization could enable targeted pruning, but the practical applicability depends on MoE adoption trends. Less directly actionable than mechanism-focused experiments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small open MoE models are less common and less well-supported than dense models. Expert activation analysis requires understanding of MoE internals. Matching active parameter count between MoE and dense is non-trivial. High complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two model architectures to finetune, plus expert activation analysis. Finding and setting up a comparable small MoE model adds overhead. The expert analysis component is a second experiment on top of the comparison.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
